Witchy Business is such a cute and charming job simulator game. I had a great time running my little witchcraft shop and feeding my cheeky kitty.

(Played on Steam Deck)

A lighthearted magical escape that lets you live your soft witch-core dreams, one potion at a time.

Who doesn’t want to run away and live their best little witchy life? Witchy Business had me sold the second I saw the art style - it’s cosy, cute, and full of magical vibes without any of the stress. From the moment the game starts, it pulls you into a calm and charming world, and even better, it lets you choose the pace of your new witchy work life. As someone who’s not always the best with time management games, being able to slow things down was perfect.

The gameplay is super simple and easy to pick up. Running on my Steam Deck was smooth with no major issues - though the charm-making mini game was a bit fiddly. Trying to draw precise lines with thumbsticks was not my finest magical moment and the touch screen has its moments.

The core loop of brewing, crafting, and selling spells is relaxing and low-stress. I’m not usually a fan of daily chore-style games, but this one keeps things varied enough to stay interesting - at least so far (I’m around 24 days in). Whether it stays fresh long-term remains to be seen, but right now the pacing feels just right.

The art style is cute as buttons. It’s cartoon-y, kawaii, and totally up the alley of anyone who loves soft witch aesthetics. The world is full of charming little touches, and I was especially happy to see that Steam achievements are shown on an in-game notice board - it’s such a nice touch for anyone who loves ticking off goals.
I could absolutely lose hours in this game. I already have, and I’ve only just started.

There isn’t a big story as such - you get hired, plopped into a magical job, and off you go. But it works. The simplicity keeps it light and easy to sink into, and the visitors to your shop are cute and quirky enough to keep the world feeling alive.

I usually turn off game music like this and play my own, but the sound design that remains is pleasant and fits the vibe. I did have a couple of moments where the sound disappeared after loading in (might be a Steam Deck thing), but nothing game-breaking.

Final Thoughts:
Witchy Business is a magical little potion shop sim that lets you craft, sell, and vibe at your own pace. It’s not deep or dramatic - it’s just plain adorable. I’d recommend it to anyone who loves cute witch-core, chill crafting games, or needs something lighthearted and easy to dip in and out of. It’s simple, sweet, and just a bit addictive.

🪄 Rating: 8/10
A cosy magical escape with charm for days - and potions to match.

Cozy Aesthetic: The hand-drawn art style and soft color palette make the game feel warm and inviting. Perfect for fans of Stardew Valley or Potionomics.

Fun Shop Management: Managing stock, customizing your shop layout, and pricing potions adds satisfying depth without being stressful.

Wholesome Story & Characters: The writing is witty and full of personality — every villager feels alive and a bit eccentric.

Relaxing Gameplay Loop: Ideal for players who enjoy slow-paced progression and chill vibes.

I went into witchy business hoping for a new cozy sim to sink into, and after a few hours I can say: it’s a delightful little potion shop adventure with plenty of charm, but it doesn’t have huge depth if you’re after a long grind.

The Good:
cozy vibe nailed – whimsical customers, cute shop decorations, and potion brewing that feels satisfying without stress.
art & music – colorful, warm visuals and a soundtrack that fits the magical, laid-back tone.
quick fun – it’s easy to pick up for a chill session; gameplay loops are simple and relaxing.

The Not-so-good:
repetition sets in – after a few hours, the loops don’t expand much. it may feel shallow for players looking for deeper progression or management.
light systems – compared to games like potionomics or recettear, there’s less complexity in upgrades or strategy.

Verdict:
If you want a short, cozy shop sim for a rainy evening, witchy business delivers exactly that. but if you’re chasing something to sink dozens of hours into, you might find it a bit thin.

Really in love with this game! Stumbled upon in whilst scrolling through the steam store, and initially looked into it because of the adorable graphics and my affinity for witchy themed things! I was surprised to see it was released so recently, it's just lovely and really well put together for the most part. Below is a Pros and Cons list of some of my biggest loves/critiques of the game so far.

Pros:
- Adorable graphics! I am in *love* with the beautiful, cutesy art style, and I also absolutely love how effortlessly diverse the characters are! The designs make the world feel full of fantastical life.
- Diverse and fun mini game mechanics. All of the shop crafting mechanics are nearly endlessly playable for me. 
- Cute NPCs with interesting flavor dialogue (though it is short).
- Multiple game difficulty modes (creative, regular, and difficult) allow for many play styles.
- You can pet the cat :3


Cons:
-The stirring mechanic for the cauldron is a bit wonky. I play with a wired mouse on laptop, and I have to move my mouse around in large awkward circles in order to get the cauldron to stir properly. I imagine it'd be an acessibiity barrier for anyone with wrist/joint issues (carpal tunnel, arthritis, etc.)
- The game is a bit short, I'd say it's about 8-10 hours of play time to 100% the game currently (Understandable, it's a brand new game, just a comment on the current available content)
- Late game, there feels like nothing to spend your currency on, as it's easy to surplus crafting items with all of the max level upgrades, so gold accumulates with nothing to do with it, and it just detracts from the game for me. I'd love to see things like in-game currency purchasable cosmetic skins to give late game players something to grind for!

Overall, I'd really recommend this game! I'm looking forward to seeing how it expands as time goes on.

Welcome back to another episode of Ele plays spooky games for spooky season! Today’s brew: Witchy Business, a cozy potion-making sim from Rogue Duck Interactive. I’ll be honest: I have mixed feelings about this dev’s catalogue (they tend to prioritize quantity over quality, cough [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3415240/Cozy_Organizer/?curator_clanid=45639970]Cozy Organizer[/url] cough), but Witchy Business still manages to deliver a decent experience if you know what you’re walking into. I played in Chaos Mode (hard difficulty), so don’t expect me to comment much on the “cozy” vibe (mine was more “panic potion simulator” during those work days).

Visually, the game is adorable, and I appreciate the accessibility option for ADHD/autism players that tones down repetitive sounds and alarms. There’s some nice variety in your witchy workday too (potions, curses, blessings, poisons, wands, and so on), plus the lack of time pressure for both crafting and shopping means you can take your time experimenting. You can upgrade nearly everything to tailor your workflow, chat with fellow witches in short little encounters, and handle everything with just your mouse (for better or worse). The instructions are clear, the loop is easy to grasp, and the first few hours can be genuinely relaxing if you enjoy repetitive, low-stress tasks.

Unfortunately, the magic fizzles out fast. The characters have as much personality as a half-stirred potion, and the story? Nonexistent. Even after several hours, I still couldn’t tell what determined product ratings, some products would earn five stars, others would tank for no reason at all. Then there are the bugs: crashes, duplicated customers, spontaneous -0.5 star penalties, and confusing item descriptions that don’t always match their function. Relationship perks in the coven unlock far too late to matter, and completionists will curse the requirement to buy every single upgrade, even obsolete ones. After about three hours in Chaos Mode, I had everything unlocked, money and reputation became meaningless, and the rest was pure grind. Some items even became momentarily unclickable because of overlapping upgrades (RIP crystal ball), and with everything being mouse-only, my wrist started a rebellion halfway through.

In the end, Witchy Business is fun while the novelty lasts, especially if you’re into simple, repetitive crafting loops. But once you hit that 3-hour mark, it turns into a cozy-looking chore simulator where your main spell is perseverance. I’d say grab it on sale or while watching a show in the background. The daily flow is built on three layers. In the sanctuary you gather herbs and minerals, in the cauldron you brew potions and craft artifacts, and finally you sell them to customers at the counter. Orders come one after another, and you must respond while handling divination, cleaning, and facility upgrades. Sometimes thieves sneak in, but you can repel them by turning them into frogs with magic. A capricious cat familiar also plays a role—its cuteness is paired with the need to feed it, adding a light sense of tension.

Difficulty can be chosen from three modes. You may enjoy harvesting and brewing at a relaxed pace, or experience a busier world where many orders and events overlap. Upgrades expand the cauldron and shop facilities, and as reputation grows, the world and events gradually change. Dangerous experiments involve risks but lead to new recipes and wands. At the bazaar, rare materials appear on a daily rotation, offering an exploratory thrill.

The visuals are colorful and hand-drawn, with UI and icons designed for clarity. Controls are mouse-based, making it easy to enjoy casually. It is a management sim full of charm that balances cuteness with busy shopkeeping.

This is one of those games that I can comfortably play first thing in the morning while sipping my coffee. It is a [i]very simple[/i], witchy store management game that is perfect to get you in the mood for a cozy, spooky season ^_^

The game play loop has you running a shop by day juggling different tasks. You are not only selling your crafted brews and relics but casting spells to ward off the bandits and telling fortunes. You get visits for custom orders, from mythical creatures who need your aid and drop off crafting materials and sometimes even shady folk visiting from Knockturn Alley. Also, bonus points because you get to feed treats to cats :D As you expand your shop, things speed up and become a bit more chaotic as you have more to manage but at no point is it stressful or punishing. If anything, it is appreciated because the initial loop is a bit boring and slow as you are standing around with nothing to do. You can up the difficulty mode if you find it a little 'too cozy'. But beware, this can only be done when you start the game. There is no option to change it later. Which is a little insane, given that I didn't realize how easy this game is on normal mode. So now I am stuck unless I want to lose all my progress. I would honestly suggest starting off harder than easier if you want it to be somewhat of a challenge. 

After the shop day, a small and limited map opens up. You can tend to a garden with options to unlock more perks, crafting materials and gold. You can visit a town vendor that gives you the opportunity to re-stock on last minute crafting materials.[spoiler] The town vendor is also a horrible little weasel. He visits your shop with the most annoying laugh trying to sell you goods at your own stall. Don’t click him. I avoid him at all costs -_- You will see!! [/spoiler] You have an alchemy station, where you craft daily through mini games. I personally like how I don't have to memorize recipes, as there is a grimoire always open to remind me what ingredients are needed. That being said, for a challenge it would be nice to have an option to turn this off. There is also a little witch council, where you can idly chat with other witches and unlock new recipes. Take note to click on everything with the exclamation mark to get free items daily and don't forget the bulletin board at the witch's council!! I didn't notice that for DAYS. It will make your life easier and gives the game a bit more substance, with quests and objectives to work towards for monetary payouts. 

While I would recommend this game, I would do so [b]ON SALE ONLY[/b]!! Given the minimalistic and repetitive nature of this game, there is no way it is worth more than $10 in my humble opinion. It is lacking in any real depth or substance to warrant the full price tag. You cannot even personally customize your character or shop, which is really disappointing.  

Visually, very beautiful game. Cute little find for the current sale price. Happy brewing, witches and warlocks!!

Witchy Business was a nice game. With some flaws, yet you acknowledge this type of games when you dive in them.

So, Witchy Business is a game about, well, witch with business: we brew and sell potions, craft wands, do some magic for clients. All while managing own garden, gathering ingredients from it or shopping for them at local shop. Game also has little relationship system with some other witches, but it was a bit too small for my full liking.

Game follows a loop of: 
-at work: take customer's orders, do future tellings, shoo off thieves and sleepwalkers, suck in a jar monster that sometimes also terrify cats, and feed cats ("you leave them hungry? rude" © familiar cat)
-after work: gather ingredients, do recieved customer orders, visit coven, tend to garden, visit shop if something is needed

Overall, game has very upfront visual artstyle: you're a witch in a pretty cute world, surrounded by cutely drawn people. A big variety of people. Music is simple at times, yet it just works. 

Also, i wasn't mistaken when decided to go for chaos difficulty: if you're someone who's used to games with a lot of management, you won't find it to difficult. Instead, you're more likely to buy some more upgrades you'll add to your management.
While the game itself is harder at first days: you don't have enough money and/or ingredients, mid to late game you will be able to accept everything. After a while i stopped doing tasks and just focused on finishing achievements

There were couple things that were not to my liking:
1. Music follows you
Sometimes after visiting shop music persists even after you leave the location. I'm not sure if it's intended or not, but such things confused me from time to time.

2. Not the best dialogues
When coven was introdusted, i was exited to know those npcs better. Tho they were pretty straight forward.. "I'm an animal witch, so i have absolutely no other characteristic to me other than i love animals". It is simple, but i craved for more deep conversations.
Also, some witches were a bit rude to us.

3. No story
We're introdusted to the world with "oh, you lost your memories due to potion". And we never get to know more. While i appreciate little notes on each character in a book, it was too little.

4. End game seemed dull
I liked how with time we were introdusted to more things: first wands, then some magic runes etc. But further you go, less info you have. And i had days where i couldn't deliver all tasks and some were expired not because i didn't do them, but because npc didn't visit due to a lot of others coming.

Overall, while game has not much story, it's a well polished game. Seeing it got halloween update, i'm looking forward for possible story updates. Game itself is not as grindy since you're the one who sets how much tasks to do. I'd give it 8/10, 6/10 if you were looking for a story.

Witchy Business, developed and published by Rogue Duck Interactive, is a charming simulation game that seamlessly blends cozy management gameplay with magical, whimsical elements. Players assume the role of a witch running their very own potion and curiosity shop, tasked with maintaining and growing the business while juggling a variety of enchanting activities. The game stands out for its engaging mechanics, colorful art style, and a playful sense of humor that makes each session feel both relaxing and rewarding.

Gameplay in Witchy Business revolves around the day-to-day management of the shop, including brewing potions, tending to a magical garden, collecting rare ingredients, and upgrading essential equipment like the alchemy station. Customers come in with diverse requests, and players must balance their time efficiently, ensuring that orders are fulfilled promptly while keeping an eye on resource management. The game also incorporates light combat elements in the form of dealing with occasional thieves, who can be hexed if they disrupt the shop’s operations. With three distinct difficulty modes—Relaxed, Casual, and Mayhem—players can tailor the experience to suit their preferred level of challenge, making the game accessible for both casual players and those seeking a more strategic management experience.

Visually, Witchy Business is a feast for the eyes, featuring hand-drawn graphics brimming with charm and personality. The environments are vibrant, from the cozy interior of the shop to the lush, magical garden outside. Character designs are expressive, and the various magical items, ingredients, and potions are beautifully detailed, adding depth to the game’s world. The dynamic soundtrack complements the visuals perfectly, creating a magical and soothing atmosphere that enhances the overall sense of immersion. Voice acting and narration add further personality, making interactions with customers and events in the game feel alive and engaging.

The game also incorporates a satisfying progression system, with opportunities to expand the shop, unlock new recipes, and earn achievements. These features encourage players to explore different strategies for managing their business and provide incentives to revisit the game multiple times. The mechanics are balanced, giving players the freedom to experiment with potion combinations and customer interactions without feeling overly constrained. Regular updates from the developers have further polished the experience, responding to player feedback to improve performance and add quality-of-life enhancements.

Overall, Witchy Business is an enchanting simulation game that successfully combines strategic management with cozy, whimsical gameplay. Its engaging mechanics, beautiful hand-drawn visuals, and charming soundtrack create a delightful experience for a wide range of players. Whether you enjoy careful planning, creative experimentation, or simply want to immerse yourself in a magical world, Witchy Business offers a unique and thoroughly enjoyable adventure that is both captivating and relaxing.

I had found this game as a demo during one of the Steam Next Fests, and it was still just as cozy to play as I had found during the demo.  

You play as a witch that owns a shop, and you go about your day managing orders, saving cats, keeping out the burglar, and waking up the sleepiest of sheep.  There is no storyline to the game outside of progressing and upgrading your shop and getting to know the witch coven, so it's really easy to just get into the swing of things and go through some mindless puzzles.  You have to plan your resources and time accordingly. and while you can go through and purchase items, the stock is random every day so there is no guarantee you'll find what you need.  There are three separate game difficulties you can choose at the beginning, and I really think that the normal gameplay should be the standard simply because the game play was easy enough to get into that going any easy would make the game too simple and boring to go through.  The 'chaos' difficulty would be interesting to try at some point, and I am glad to have that available in the game.

The art is very cute and simplistic, and I love the designs that were put into everything in the game.  It definitely gives off that everything was hand-drawn and animated with that in mind.  The music is a very pleasant background noise, and every location has different music set to it.  Considering it is the same track, it can get boring after a bit since it's on a constant loop.  

I did really enjoy the differences between the different witches you meet, though you don't get to talk to them a whole lot.  The dialogue options you choose do affect your relationships with them though, so it can take a while to earn their full trust!  I wish there was an option to have journal entries for each of the witches outside of the small blurb you learn from their image in the journal though.

The achievements were a very nice range from easy to difficult, though it gets easier to get them the longer you play.  Nothing was truly difficult to get, which makes achievement hunting easy enough they can be achieved within a single play through.

Overall, I do very much love this game and love how easily you can get into playing it.  Since there is no active storyline, you don't have to worry about the replayability, though it isn't really a game you can spend countless hours playing because of how simple the controls can be.  Definitely a game I would recommend playing, but I don't think the game is worth $15.

Cute graphics, but the gameplay blows right now. 

The most prominent mechanic you have to make use of, stirring the cauldron to finish off your potions, frequently doesn't properly register mouse movements. It either doesn't recognize your attempts to stir at all, causing the gauge to not move; or it suddenly jumps up half the gauge with the barest movement, usually right at the end of the time allotted, forcing you into the red zone and with no time for the gauge to ease back down. There's also times where the spoon/ladle comes up out of the cauldron and then doesn't want to go back down, ruining whatever momentum you had. It's extremely frustrating to try dealing with. Wand making and cursing items mini-games are very basic, far less mechanics to potentially go wrong with, and therefore work fine.

The flow of customers and incidents happening at your stall is a frantic rush from the very beginning, instead of building up as your reputation increases and would cause a greater demand for your wares. Which is especially problematic in the early game when certain spirits or customers that the tutorial didn't cover the mechanics for show up and start ticking down your reputation, or a gauge is steadily dropping to indicate you're about to lose out on whatever reward they have to offer, and you're hurrying to try all your tools on them to figure out which will interact- all while other customers or a thief or other spirits are popping up and have their own things going, and random dirt spots are suddenly popping up, and your familiar is demanding to be fed yet again. The devs are trying to jam way too much into a very short day cycle that's a mere two minutes long. Extending out the day an extra minute or two to pace things a little better would be far more player friendly.

There's plenty of ways to gain herbs, including growing your own in your tiny garden, and the bazaar seems to favor selling them or oddities. Trying to keep up your stock of minerals, however, especially the silver and gold ores during my playthrough, can be very difficult. The RNG seems to hate offering them up, and it becomes a severe bottleneck for what potions you can make.

The interactions with other witches once the coven unlocks are also shallow to the extreme. They say a single sentence, you have a 2-6 word response to give back, and then they giggle and you're done for the day. Repeat for the second witch present. Done again. That's it. There's no real sense of who these other witches are or why you should care about gaining their favor. Given how little plot there is elsewhere to drive the gameplay, no story besides the vague starting concept of "run your own witch business", the lack of NPC characterization is all the more starkly apparent.

The idea for this game is intriguing, and the concepts for the gameplay loop and mini games are good in theory, but this supposed full release game feels like a bare bones Early Access entry. It needs a lot of gameplay tweaks and UI fixes, and preferably an injection of some actual plot/character content, before I could consider recommending it to anyone.

Nobody talks to you, except at the coven - and even there, it feels like every character has four sentences total to share with you, and they WILL repeat themselves.

I found it interesting that my character was called [spoiler]the basic witch[/spoiler] and then raised my eyebrows at how completely at odds this was with the fact that as soon as my reputation hit a certain threshold [spoiler]I was suddenly promoted to the leader of the coven[/spoiler]. It's a nice-looking game but... beyond the cute art, it seems to have no soul at all.

My game time is also bloated, because clicking the "save and exit" button seems to neither save nor exit the game. Instead you land in the main menu, with some progress lost unless you did time it with the beginning of the day (where the game saves automatically). I find that rude, as far as game design goes.

If i could give a medium review with the thumbs up i would. I enjoyed this game and got 8 hours in but after a few hours it became pretty boring. The days loop almost exactly the same routine day in day out. The secret potions were quick and easy to figure out and complete, the only thing that kept me going after that was the steam achievements. 

It felt like there was something missing like another area available on the map or having something else to do other than the same routine over and over. The relationship levels became a grind finding myself not interested in what they had to say because you dont really form a bond or relationship with them its just one liners and they dont really react. The graphics are cute and the game was enjoyable but became boring fast there's something missing that would push it to the next level to make it more interesting. it's lacking something that would pull you out of the groundhog day feeling like maybe missions that involved visiting other people and delivering the potions and wands or having a home to go to to decorate. I dont know what it needs but it needs something else. It did not feel worth the price sorry

It was fun at first, but it became boring pretty quickly. I really thought they were going to add additional story (like a visual novel aspect) with the addition of the other witches (possible friendship / love interest routes, for example — it didn’t have to be complex, a simple story for each of the witches would have been nice), but there was barely anything. It’s a cozy, clicker game and that’s it — if that’s your thing, that’s cool! I totally get it if people dig this kinda thing. But for me, I wouldn’t really recommend this game, ESPECIALLY for that high of a price. Please get it on a discount for the sake of your wallet. :,)

The game is what I'd consider mediocre for the price. Pretty barebones but you can get some entertainment from it. Cute game, but it's just a clicker that doesn't require much effort. Once you unlock everything, even the 'Hard' difficulty feels too easy. Like most of their other games I own (Ship Inc., Cozy Organizer), it's very buggy. Items will go missing in the garden, and sometimes you get -1✮ even after doing something correctly.

When I reached out for support, I was told to join their Discord server — but when I did, I was completely ignored. I'll just play this as an idler or when I'm really bored. Definitely not worth the full price — grab it on a discount (as low as possible).
